chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, all from Safwan from Sa'id al-A'raj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about two men who had intercourse with a young girl during one period of purity (tahur), to whom does the child belong? He said: 'To the one who has the girl, based on the saying of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): The child belongs to the bed (the one who has her), and for the adulterer is the stone.'

key_terms.الْحَجَرُ: The stone (symbolizing the penalty or exclusion of lineage)
key_terms.طُهْرٍ: Period of purity between menstrual cycles
key_terms.لِلْفِرَاشِ: To the bed (metaphor for the primary partner/owner)

ai.seo_question: Who is the father of a child if two men have intercourse with the same girl during one period of purity?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the application of the principle 'al-waladu lil-firash' (the child belongs to the bed) in cases of polyandrous uncertainty, specifically when a girl under the guardianship of one man has intercourse with multiple men during a single period of purity. The ruling attributes lineage to the primary possessor (the one with the right of access), reflecting the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the stability of family structures and the presumption of paternity based on the most likely scenario. This principle is rooted in the broader prophetic tradition distinguishing between the legitimate partner and the adulterer, ensuring clear lineage attribution even in complex marital or guardianship contexts.
